{{Short description|American mathematician (1918–2004)}}
'''Robert Clarke James''' (1918<ref>{{cite book |last1=James |first1=Robert C. |last2=James |first2=Glenn |title=Mathematics Dictionary |date=1992 |publisher=Chapman & Hall |location=New York |isbn=0412990415 |edition=5th}}  On copyright page.</ref> – September 25, 2004)<ref name="MuddMath"/> was an [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]] who worked in [[functional analysis]].

==Biography==
James attended [[UCLA]] as an undergraduate, where his father was a professor.  As a devout [[Quakers|Quaker]], he was a [[conscientious objector]] during [[World War II]].<ref name="MuddMath"/>

He obtained his PhD at [[Caltech]] in 1946 under the direction of Aristotle Demetrius Michal.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|10376}}</ref>  He spent a year as a Benjamin Peirce Fellow at [[Harvard University|Harvard]] and joined the faculty at [[UC Berkeley]].  In 1950, during the [[History of the University of California, Berkeley#1950s|loyalty oath controversy]], James refused to sign the oath and moved to [[Haverford College]].  Later he was the founding math department chair both at [[Harvey Mudd College]] and at the [[Claremont Graduate University]].<ref name="MuddMath">{{cite magazine| first1=Joseph |last1=Platt |author-link1=Joseph Platt (university president) |first2=Robin and Lori |last2=Ives |title=Robert James, Founding Mathematics Chair |magazine=MuddMath |date=Spring 2005 |volume=4 |issue=1 |url=https://www.hmc.edu/mathematics/wp-content/uploads/sites/49/2017/07/v4n1.pdf}}</ref>

James constructed a number of counterexamples in the theory of [[Banach space]]s, including [[James' space]] and [[James' tree space]].  He also characterized [[reflexive space|reflexivity]] for Banach spaces with an [[Schauder basis#Unconditionality|unconditional Schauder basis]] and proved an [[James' theorem|eponymous compactness criterion]].

With his father {{ill|Glenn James (mathematician)|lt=Glenn James|de|Glenn James}} (a professor at [[UCLA]] and long-time editor of [[Mathematics Magazine]]) he published a mathematical dictionary which went through several editions.<ref>{{cite web |title=University of California: In Memoriam, April 1962. Glenn James, Mathematics: Los Angeles |url=https://oac.cdlib.org/view?docId=hb0b69n6g4&doc.view=frames&chunk.id=div00006&toc.depth=1&toc.id=&brand=calisphere |website=California Digital Library |access-date=19 September 2022}}</ref>

James was made a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |title=Historic Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic |website=www.aaas.org |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science |access-date=19 September 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
